lead: Hyperliquid’s daily volume returned to the $10 billion range as liquidity concentrated at leading venues and the dispute between CME and the CFTC over US perpetual futures intensified.

threads.title: CME v. CFTC: US classification of perpetuals
threads.update: **Today:** CME argues that perpetuals should be regulated as swaps rather than futures and accuses the CFTC of rubber-stamping Kalshi's first US perpetual futures contract. This is the second development since June 19.
threads.watch: Hearing dates, whether CME seeks a preliminary injunction, and the CFTC's response

items.headline: Hyperliquid's daily volume returns to the $10 billion range
body: **Event:** Daily volume on Hyperliquid exceeded $10 billion, within the $5 billion to $15 billion range used for leading protocols. Its estimated share of DEX volume was 60–75%.

**Mechanism:** New markets drew more active addresses, while fees funded buybacks. The interaction between activity and price increased concentration among DEXs and added pressure on mid-sized protocols.

context.label: Scale
context.text: The sample's 4–10% benchmark for DEX perpetuals differs from the 60–75% cited above. The figures are unreconciled. One day cannot establish a shift.

items.headline: Fee revenue diverges at GMX and dYdX
items.body: GMX fee revenue held steady. Following changes to incentives on dYdX v4, the protocol earned less in fees than in the previous period. Annualized LP yields fell as volatility eased.

items.headline: Lighter adjusts risk limits for volatile markets
body: **Event:** Lighter tightened initial margin requirements and position limits for volatile pairs.
**Mechanism:** Limits vary by market depth and volatility. Adding markets requires setting appropriate parameters for each pair instead of applying a single leverage schedule.

items.headline: pump.fun introduces creator fee sharing
items.body: Token creators can earn a share of trading activity under revised migration rules. GMGN updated its smart-money labels.

items.headline: Four.meme revises token migration thresholds
items.body: The new conditions distinguish bonding-curve trading from the preparation of external liquidity to reduce failures during migration.

items.headline: Moonshot adds creator fee disclosures
items.body: Token pages show creator fees and migration status before a trade, making those terms easier to check.

items.headline: BTC trades near the top of its range as ETH strengthens
items.body: Spot ETF flows turned positive as risk appetite recovered slightly.

items.headline: Coinbase expands regulated derivatives coverage
items.body: The new contracts let more spot customers access margin trading from the same account.

items.headline: A tokenized securities platform expands on-chain transfers
items.body: Holders can transfer eligible tokenized assets between compliant accounts and self-custody wallets, expanding on-chain distribution.

items.headline: AI coding agents receive a series of tooling updates
items.body: Several vendors expanded context windows and improved tool-call reliability. Developers reported lower integration costs.

items.headline: Trading agents add auditable tool-call records
items.body: Agents retain structured records of searches, quotes and order requests so reviewers can trace errors to their source.

items.headline: Agent tools add human approval steps
items.body: High-risk actions can pause for human approval before execution, limiting the impact of accidental trades.
